stem: The lymphatic drainage of the liver primarily drains into:
fact: Hepatic lymph drains through hepatic nodes to coeliac nodes.
finding: NCBI and PMC evidence support the displayed key.

stem: The rectus sheath encloses all of the following structures except the:
fact: The rectus sheath contains rectus and pyramidalis, epigastric vessels, and terminal thoracic nerves; transversus abdominis is not enclosed.
mnemonic: Rectus sheath surrounds rectus, not transversus.
finding: NCBI abdominal-wall anatomy supports the exception.

stem: The ilioinguinal nerve supplies skin over which of the following regions:
fact: The ilioinguinal nerve supplies the upper medial thigh and external genitalia.

stem: The greater sac of the peritoneal cavity is divided into two compartments by which of the following structures:
fact: The transverse mesocolon divides the greater sac into supracolic and infracolic compartments.
mnemonic: Transverse mesocolon makes the upper/lower split.
finding: Standard peritoneal anatomy supports the source explanation.

stem: Which of the following areas of the prostate gland is the most commonly involved in prostatic hyperplasia:
fact: Benign prostatic hyperplasia primarily expands the transitional zone around the prostatic urethra.
mnemonic: BPH grows in the transition zone.
finding: NCBI and PMC evidence support transitional-zone involvement.

stem: The ilioinguinal nerve innervates which of the following muscles:
options: Internal oblique and transversus abdominis muscles
Transversus abdominis and rectus abdominis muscles
fact: The ilioinguinal nerve supplies internal oblique and transversus abdominis.
finding: Source explanation supports the displayed key.

stem: Which of the following best describes the position of the temporal lobe:
options: Anterior to the central sulcus and superior to the lateral sulcus
Posterior to the central sulcus and superior to the lateral sulcus
fact: The temporal lobe lies inferior to the lateral sulcus.
mnemonic: Temporal is below the lateral fissure.
finding: Standard cerebral topography supports the displayed key.

stem: A 31 year old male presents to ED with a head injury. Rhinorrhoea will most likely result from fracture of which of the following bones:
fact: Ethmoid cribriform-plate fracture can cause CSF rhinorrhoea.
finding: NCBI CSF-leak and cribriform-fracture pages support ethmoid.

stem: The primary motor cortex is located in which of the following regions:
fact: The primary motor cortex lies in the precentral gyrus of the frontal lobe.
mnemonic: Motor starts in the frontal precentral gyrus.
finding: Standard cortical anatomy supports the displayed key.

stem: A 74 year old man presents with a three month history of worsening left shoulder and arm pain. On examination there is weakness of shoulder abduction and reduced sensation over the deltoid. You suspect cervical radiculopathy. What level of the cervical spine is most likely to be affected:
fact: C5 involvement produces deltoid weakness and sensory change over the deltoid region.
mnemonic: C5 drives shoulder abduction via deltoid.
finding: The clinical pattern and source explanation support C5.
